items.title: New Official Cyberpunk Release Leaked
items.summary: A new release based on the Cyberpunk series apparently leaks ahead of an official announcement from CD Projekt Red and the developers.
items.content:
New Official Cyberpunk Release Leaked From GameRant (Written by Marc Deschamps) on July 29, 2026 | OpenCritic

Cyberpunk 2077 fans might have a new release to look forward to, as an upcoming game has apparently leaked ahead of an announcement from CD Projekt Red. Cyberpunk 2077 has been a big success since its release in 2020, selling more than 40 million copies. Fans have been eager for more ways to explore the game's world over the last six years, and CD Projekt Red seems to have multiple projects in development.

While fans eagerly await more content, the current game has shown no signs of slowing down. Cyberpunk 2077 hit a new peak player count in June, with the highest Steam concurrent numbers since the game's Phantom Liberty DLC was released in 2023. It's unclear whether that interest will carry over to future games, but it does bode well for CD Projekt Red.

Mike Pondsmith, the creator of the Cyberpunk tabletop RPG, says he has "ways" to make Keanu Reeves' Johnny Silverhand return in the 2077 sequel.

According to a new leak, CD Projekt Red and WayFoward Technologies teamed up for a game based on the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime series. The game's existence was leaked through the portfolio of a former WayForward employee, and it was apparently in...

items.title: New 'Cyberpunk' Game Leaks Online—Here's What Project 'Gemini' Will Bring to the Franchise
items.summary: The Cyberpunk franchise is reportedly delivering a new game codenamed Project Gemini, according to the latest leak.
items.content:
Steam, CD Projekt Red A previously unknown " Cyberpunk " project has surfaced through a former developer's portfolio, revealing that CD Projekt Red quietly partnered with a third-party developer on a new title under the franchise.

According to MP1st , who first spotted the portfolio, the unannounced project was codenamed Project Gemini, an R&D effort worked on at WayForward between 2025 and early 2026.

That R&D label typically signals early-stage development, a phase where studios prototype mechanics and test technical frameworks before committing to full production, meaning the project's current status remains unclear and could easily have been scrapped.

The portfolio described Project Gemini as a "rollback-driven" 2.5D brawler, a genre that blends flat, side-scrolling gameplay with three-dimensional character models and environments.

That description brings to mind WayForward's previous work on the "River City Girls" series, and an internal project logo reportedly paired the "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners" branding directly alongside the Gemini codename. This key information reinforces the connection to the Netflix anime spinoff.

According to GameRant , WayForward is best known for developing the "Shantae" series, along with its more recent "River City Girls" brawlers. The developer's notes reportedly referenced a "rollback-safe architecture" and "online transport integration," suggesting Project Gemini was being built with online multiplayer and rollback netcode in mind.

This development focus is similar to the systems found in WayForward's latest "River City Girls" entry.

Separately, MP1st noted that WayForward had another unannounced Unreal Engine 5 project in development based on a licensed IP. This project reached a vertical slice before funding delays halted its progress and led to layoffs at the studio last September.

Whether that separate UE5 project was actually Project Gemini remains unconfirmed, though the timelines for both overlap closely enough to raise the possibility. Even if the "Cyberpunk" R&D effort was ultimately shelved, the pitch itself shows CD Projekt Red was actively exploring ways to expand the "Edgerunners" IP beyond the screen.

CD Projekt Red has already confirmed its next major "Cyberpunk" title, known as Project Orion or "Cyberpunk 2," as the direct sequel to 2020's "Cyberpunk 2077." Project Gemini is an entirely separate, unconfirmed concept rather than any version of that mainline sequel.

Instead, Project Gemini would function as a spinoff tied specifically to "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners," the acclaimed Netflix animated series produced by Studio Trigger that helped drive renewed interest in the franchise following its 2022 debut.

A new season of "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners " is set to return later this year. However, it remains unknown which characters from the show's expanding cast Project Gemini would have centered on, since the series has continued introducing new leads beyond its original protagonist.

CD Projekt Red has previously looked outside its own studio for spinoff projects too, including reported interest in partnering with Scopely on a multiplayer "Witcher" game, showing a broader pattern of the company exploring external collaborations to expand its core franchises.

items.title: CD Projekt Red is reportedly working on a secret Cyberpunk game, but there's a plot twist
items.summary: The hit anime based on Cyberpunk 2077 is rumored to have had a game of its own
items.content:
By Willa Rowe Published Jul 28, 2026, 2:00 PM EDT News Gemini would be a 2.5D brawler based on the hit anime

Resident Evil 2 is now officially the series' best-selling game Henry Cavill’s Warhammer 40K universe at Prime Video gets major update as horror master joins team Ubisoft's scraps Far Cry extraction shooter for 'really ambitious' open-world FPS, report says Cyberpunk: Edgerunners game was reportedly in development, but its future is uncertain Image: Studio Trigger/Netflix Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Sign in to your Polygon.com account CD Projekt Red has already confirmed it's hard at work on a Cyberpunk 2077 sequel, codenamed Project Orion , but that might not be the only video game in development. It has now been reported that a game based on the anime Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is also in the works.

The game, codenamed Gemini , is reportedly a 2.5D brawler inspired by the hit anime from Studio Trigger, set in the Cyberpunk universe. According to MP1st , the game was being developed by WayForward, the studio behind River City Girls and Shantae. Details on Gemini were discovered in a former WayForward developer's portfolio, which describes the project as a rollback-driven brawler in development between 2025 and 2026. The portfolio also labeled the project as a CDPR title in the R&D phase. Also included was an internal logo that features the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners branding with the Gemini name included.

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners has arguably seen more success than the RPG on which it is based. While Cyberpunk 2077 took years to rectify a disastrous launch, Studio Trigger's anime was met with widespread critical acclaim when it was released in 2022. Since then, Edgerunners has crossed over with other games. Anime favorite Lucy became a playable character in the fighting game Guilty Gear Strive and the gacha game Wuthering Waves . It would make sense for CD Projekt Red to capitalize on the property's popularity with a game of its own. A second season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is due to be released this fall .

Further reports indicate that WayForward had an unannounced project in 2025 whose development was halted. The studio then underwent a round of layoffs last September. If that unannounced project was in fact Gemini , then the game may no longer be in active development. With only the portfolio details to go on, it is unclear what the fate of Gemini is.

Polygon has reached out to CD Projekt Red and WayForward for comment.

By Rhiannon Bevan Published Jul 28, 2026, 12:55 PM EDT Rhiannon (she/her) is the Deputy News Lead and Chief Reporter at TheGamer. You may have heard her on the BBC or read her words at TechRadar Gaming and TechRaptor . She won MCV's Journalism Impact for Women in Games in 2025. At TheGamer, you will often find her chatting to game developers, writers, and actors about their crafts. This includes a deep dive into Cyberpunk 2077's narrative , and a series on the making of the Fable trilogy . She also follows industrial action and existential threats to its workers, particularly the use of generative AI. As part of this, she's explored how AI Darth Vader sets a dangerous precedent , and was one of the first reporters to look into generative AI dating companions . Sign in to your TheGamer account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap CD Projekt Red reportedly greenlit a Cyberpunk 2077 spin-off, partnering with indie devs to make it happen. This spin-off was said to be based on the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime and would have been a very different genre from the main game.

This is according to information gathered by MP1st . Citing a developer’s portfolio, MP1st says that CDPR was working with WayForward, best known for Shantae and River City Girls, on this spin-off. The game would have reportedly been a brawler, featuring characters from Edgerunners.

As per the report, the developer (who MP1st has kept anonymous) lists an “unannounced CDPR Cyberpunk R&D project” on their resume. The project was codenamed “Gemini”, with the dev saying they worked on it from 2025-26. It’s unclear if this means the game was cancelled, or if this is just when the dev left WayForward.

The game is described as a 2.5D brawler, like River City Girls. Mentions of rollback and online play make it clear it was being made with multiplayer in mind - something that would be new for the Cyberpunk series.

This would line up with what CDPR has done with the series since Cyberpunk 2077’s launch. When Edgerunners proved to be a hit, its cast of characters started to pop up in other games, including a recent Wuthering Waves event . It would make sense for CDPR to capitalise on this even further by publishing a brand new game with David, Lucy, and the rest of the gang as playable characters. A brawler would be a good fit for them, too.

CDPR has also opened itself up to outsourcing projects in recent years. The remake of the first Witcher game is being handled by Fool’s Theory, while recent Cyberpunk 2077 updates were rolled out thanks to Virtuos. This is likely to keep the franchises alive in between mainline entries, since development times are only getting longer.

Even if this fighting game was cancelled, it at least tells us that CDPR saw the value in an Edgerunners game at some point. While we wait to see if anything comes of that, we’re finally getting another season of Edgerunners this fall .

items.title: A Cyberpunk Spin-Off Brawler Might Be Happening At WayForward – Report
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.5 Brawler Reportedly in Development From CD Projekt and Shantae Studio WayForward
items.summary: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is being turned into a 2.5D brawler by Shantae developer WayForward, it's been reported.
items.content:
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is being turned into a 2.5D brawler by Shantae developer WayForward, it's been reported.

Edgerunners, the acclaimed anime spin-off from CD Projekt's Cyberpunk 2077, is set to return soon for more episodes — but there's even more from its world on the way. That's according to a report by MP1st , which has lifted the lid on an unannounced project codenamed "Gemini" that has been in development since 2025.

Details gleaned from an unnamed former WayForward employee point to the project being in the research and design phase — so still some way from launching. Still, the game has apparently been planned as a "rollback-driven" 2.5D brawler, potentially similar to WayForward's River City Girls series — which also has an anime vibe.

What's unclear now is whether the project remains in development. MP1st reports that WayForward had an unannounced game based on an external franchise cancelled last year after losing funding, leading to layoffs last September — but it's unknown if this project was Gemini, or something else.

CD Projekt declined to comment on the matter when contacted by IGN today.

And, of course, even if Gemini does not ultimately see a release, Cyberpunk fans can look forward to a second season of Edgerunners — which is currently set to premiere on Netflix this fall. Fans have already been analyzing a recent trailer to try and work out where the new episodes will be set . You can also read about how Season 1 nearly had an even sadder ending than the one it got .

On the video game front, Cyberpunk 2 is in development, with 163 people working on it as of the end of April. While we know little about the sequel, Cyberpunk creator Mike Pondsmith teased some details when he was asked about the scope of his involvement with what was then known as Project Orion, back at the Digital Dragons 2025 conference.

In September last year, speaking with IGN while promoting his movie Good Fortune, Keanu Reeves said that he wanted to be part of the Cyberpunk sequel . “Absolutely. I’d love to play Johnny Silverhand again," Reeves said when asked if he’d be interested in revisiting his legendary rockstar terrorist character in Cyberpunk 2. Pondsmith later said he'd worked out a way to make it make sense , and has told the much-loved actor: “contact me.”

It sounds like we'll have to wait some time to find out. CD Projekt is of course focusing on The Witcher 4, and Nowakowski has suggested Cyberpunk 2 won’t be out until at least 2030. Perhaps that's why Cyberpunk 2077 fans have called on CD Projekt to change its mind and release more DLC for the game , as it is with The Witcher 3.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: Rumour: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Game Was, and Still Might Be, in Development at a Surprising Studio
items.content:
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners , the hit anime based on the existing Cyberpunk universe and branching off from Cyberpunk 2077 , might be getting its own video game project.

This is according to a new report from MP1st , who claim that an unnamed source was, at some point, working on an Edgerunners adaptation, in collaboration with 2077 developer CD Projekt Red.

The truly interesting part, though, is that the source was employed at WayForward — the longstanding Californian company behind the Shantae games, River City Girls 2 , and much more.

It's said that this Edgerunners project — codenamed Gemini — was actually a 2.5D brawler, so partnering with WayForward, with its side-scrolling and beat-'em-up expertise, suddenly makes a lot of sense.

But here's the thing: it's currently unclear whether this title ever got off the ground. The source no longer works at WayForward, although the project was in some form of production as recently as this year.

So while I would advise against getting your hopes up that this thing will ever release, it's still really interesting that CD Projekt Red was seemingly so keen to spin Edgerunners off into its own game.

It's possible that more information on 'Gemini' will surface over the coming weeks and months now that this report is doing the rounds.

Would you have been up for an Edgerunners brawler? Just imagine the potential levels of gore in the comments section below.

items.title: Report: CD Projekt Red Partnered With Shantae Devs on a 2.5D Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Brawler
items.summary: We have learned that the team behind the Shantae series had been working on a 2.5D Cyberpunk: Edgerunners brawler in partnership with CDPR.
items.content:
CD Projekt Red has been hard at work expanding the Cyberpunk 2077 universe. Alongside Project Orion, the highly anticipated sequel to the 2020 game, fans are also looking forward to a new season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, the acclaimed Netflix animated spin-off produced by Studio Trigger that is set to return this year.

However, those might not be the only titles in the pipeline for the dystopian franchise. We have discovered that CDPR had been collaborating with WayForward, the studio best known for the Shantae series, on a smaller side game based on the aforementioned spin-off show.

Details on this previously unknown project originate from the portfolio of a former WayForward developer, whose name we are withholding for privacy reasons. The developer’s resume details an unannounced CDPR Cyberpunk R&D project codenamed ‘Gemini’ that was in the works at WayForward between 2025 and 2026.

Given this timeframe and the R&D label, it is safe to say the game was in the very early stages of development. This label typically represents a phase where studios prototype mechanics, build technical frameworks, and test concepts before greenlighting full production.

Unfortunately, the developer’s resume doesn’t clarify the project’s current status, which could easily mean it’s a scrapped concept. Despite this, the portfolio provides some interesting tidbits regarding the dev’s contributions, including an internal project logo that features the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners branding right alongside the “Gemini” codename.

Based on the brief description provided on the website, Project Gemini was conceptualized as a “rollback-driven” 2.5D brawler. This immediately brings to mind WayForward’s previous work on the River City Girls franchise. Considering that both the game series and Edgerunners share a high-energy anime aesthetic, blending the show’s universe into a 2.5D beat-’em-up certainly feels fitting.

Beyond the brawler premise, the developer’s notes reveal a few noteworthy technical features. Mentions of a “rollback-safe architecture” and “online transport integration” indicate that the game was being built with online multiplayer and rollback netcode in mind, features also included in River City Girls’ latest entry.

Separate findings also reveal that WayForward had an unannounced Unreal Engine 5 project in the works based on a licensed IP. The team delivered a vertical slice for this project, but according to a developer, funding was delayed, leading to halted development and a round of layoffs at the studio in September of last year.

Whether or not this specific project was Gemini remains unknown, though we do know the mystery UE5 title was in active development during at least 2025. This timeline aligns closely, given that the Cyberpunk title was worked on through early 2026 according to the portfolio data. Even if the R&D project was ultimately cancelled during strategic realignments, the pitch alone shows that CDPR was actively looking to expand the Edgerunners IP beyond the screen.

This wouldn’t be the first time CDPR has looked outside its own walls to build on its core franchises. We previously reported on the Polish publisher’s interest in partnering with external developers, such as Scopely’s potential involvement in a multiplayer Witcher game for PC and mobile devices . It remains to be seen if that title will beat CDPR to the punch before the studio releases its own in-house multiplayer spin-off, Project Sirius.

Stay connected to MP1st and the latest news by following us on Bluesky , X , Facebook , TikTok , YouTube , and Google News .

items.content:
Lovecraftian misadventures, cat-breeding tactics games and, of course, Thief.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Raphaël Colantonio/CD Projekt Red) Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Disk Cleanup

Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Raphaël Colantonio became a PC gamer for a very specific reason—he was a huge Ultima fan and wanted to play Ultima 7. "Number six did not come out on Apple. It was so painful to me, the idea I could not play Ultima, that I bought a PC," says the co-founder of Arkane Studios. "It ended up being exactly what I wanted, because it [had] way more possibilities than any of the Ultimas until then."

After working at companies like EA and Infogrames, in 1999 Colantonio co-founded Arkane Studios. The studio's debut game was Arx Fatalis, a first-person RPG inspired by Looking Glass' genre-redefining Ultima Underworld . Over the next two decades, Arkane established itself as the modern successor to Looking Glass, developing some of the PC's best games, such as 2012's Dishonored and 2017's Prey .

Following Prey's release, Colantonio left Arkane to establish WolfEye studios, which published its first game— Weird West —in 2022. WolfEye is currently working on an unnamed first-person RPG—though it may actually have a name now, at least internally. "I think we have it," Colantonio says.

Colantonio took a break from WolfEye's next project for a rooftop reconnaissance of his Steam library. We discussed tactical cats, dystopian decision-making, and ripping off the tech behind the world's greatest stealth game.

The one that I'm playing right now is Mewgenics .

Bennett Foddy, designer of QWOP and Baby Steps, is obsessed with friendslop games and won't uninstall Baldur's Gate 3, even though he'll probably never finish it: 'It was too big and so I stopped' 'The mid-2000s was the golden era of first-person shooters': David Szymanski, creator of Dusk and Iron Lung, discusses the games on his PC 'I try to play as a completionist and leave no stone unturned and no enemy unkilled': Returnal director Harry Krueger talks Deus Ex, Resident Evil, and the arcade classic that inspired Housemarque's best games I played Mewgenics because I was a big fan of The Binding of Isaac , and I just bought it with eyes closed, not knowing what I was getting into, and initially I was disappointed because it felt like a very different game than what I was expecting. I thought it would be action, and instead it was more like a turn-based combat game.

They have this metagame that I don't think works super well. I'm not exactly sure what I'm doing with my cats, like, how can I actually benefit from their legacies to create better cats? To me, so far, this part is very blurry. I'm just waiting day-by-day [for] the new cats [to] come in and then some of them die.

But then it kind of grew on me over time, and I think some of it was, [it] kept me in by the rage in some ways, and by the fun in some other ways, because it had to be fun enough that I wanted to see more, and [it has] some really cool combo[s] because it is a little bit in the style of The Binding of Isaac … it's almost like it relies on not being tuned. So you can have an absolutely shitty run, or you can have this incredibly OP run, which feels super satisfying until you die or make a mistake.

I was thinking, what other [tactics] games did I play that I put a lot of hours in? Into the Breach was one of them, which is definitely on the tactics side. I would say XCOM also was a big one for me. Those are not games that I would be good at designing, but I enjoy playing them.

Developer CD Projekt Red announced the title as being in development back in 2012, as the follow-up property after The Witcher series.

As the studio’s next step after the genre-defining action/adventure role-playing game (RPG) The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt , Cyberpunk 2077 has big shoes to fill. Teasers, trailers, an intriguing (and beautiful) gameplay demo and industry buzz as it has been built have only increased the sense of anticipation that something truly special is on its way.

The buzz has been set to a fever pitch by way of the trailers and demos walking away with an almost embarrassing number of awards, even before launch - over one hundred awards at E3 2018. They include Best PC Game, Best RPG, Best Game, Best Xbox One Game, People's Choice (IGN), both Best RPG and Game of the Show ( Game Informer ), Game of the Show (GamesRadar+), and Best of E3 ( PC Gamer ) [1]

But it is not just since 2012 that the idea for such a video game has been around. In a way, it is actually 32 years in the making . It’s altogether fitting and perhaps even somewhat poetic that the release date for a Cyberpunk video game has been set for 2020. The Cyberpunk 2077 release date is April 16, 2020, to be specific.

This is because the photo-realistic, CGI graphics, global-network-internet-distributed video game is based on a late 80s tabletop, pen-and-paper roleplaying game, created by Mike Pondsmith, called Cyberpunk 2020. That game imagined our present moment of 2020 as a corporate dystopian future, filled with network computers and cybercrime.

Cyberpunk 2077 , which was developed with the tabletop game creator Pondsmith as a story/world-building consultant, puts itself 57 years past the setting of the original, boxed pen-and-paper game, and is released in the actual year imagined as “far off and futuristic” when that game was created. It was not until the present moment - imagined as the far-off future - that such a video game realization of those 1988 ideas could exist.

The original pen-and-paper, tabletop roleplaying game (think “Dungeons and Dragons” meets a William Gibson novel) imagined a fictional metropolis called Night City, somewhere between LA and San Francisco. Night City in 2020 existed in a United States that had undergone both socio-economic collapse and a period of martial law and turned to the “mega-corporations” to survive.

The mega-corporations are military, tech, media, petro-chemical, weapons, and industrial companies and conglomerates that vie for dominance and compete to rule the world by any means necessary. Meanwhile, street gangs and black markets also run rampant.

Set against this backdrop, characters take on roles like “Netrunners,” “Med-Techs,” “Nomads,” and “Fixers.” These characters are employed as freelance mercenaries contracted out for industrial sabotage or spying or to take on and take down the plots and machinations of the various mega-corporations.

Cyberpunk 2077 fast forwards 57 years and puts the player in the central and starring role of “V.” Just who this protagonist is, much like a character you might play in a table-top RPG, is up to you, the player.

A good deal of the buzz about Cyberpunk 2077 has to do with how CD Projekt Red has crafted a seamless, cinematic adventure game, complete with cutscenes and dialogue, where the entire look, gender, and even background of the main character are customizable.

You very much determine how your particular experience of the game is going to be by way of the character you craft V to be; your V (and your gameplay) can and will be markedly different than another person’s.

Depending on what gender, hairstyle, clothing, and character background you choose (your V can be either a nomad, a street kid, or corporate in his or her back story), the game and the non-player characters (NPCs) who populate it will react differently to you, and different quests and pathways will open or close.

Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.

items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]

items.content:
Surviving the City of Dreams is tough, but a choom at your side can make all the difference.

In our latest It’s All About You episode, we’re celebrating all of our iconic duos living on the edge! Night City wouldn’t shine quite so bright without them. 

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners in the most creative ways possible. Don't forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY. See you in the next episode!

items.title: Update 2.3 Patch Notes
items.summary: Update 2.3 lands tomorrow! Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as sup
items.content:
Update 2.3 lands tomorrow!

Experience Night City in a whole new way — this patch introduces 4 new vehicles, the AutoDrive feature, self-driving Delamain cabs and more! It also contains updates for CrystalCoat™ and Photo Mode, as well as support for AMD FSR 3.1 Frame Generation, Intel XeSS 2.0 and HDR10+ Gaming, among others.

Update 2.3 also brings Cyberpunk 2077 to a whole new platform: Mac with Apple silicon! If you already own the game on Steam, you can play it on your compatible device. To find out whether your Mac can run Cyberpunk 2077, please check the official requirements.

Read the list of changes for more info:

Vehicles

  • Added 4 new vehicles, including several Side Jobs tied to acquiring them:

    • Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Hunt and The Beast In Me).

      An additional side job unlocks the CrystalCoat™ feature for it.

      [/*]

    • Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred"

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, complete The Beast in Me: Badlands, The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo, Transmission, and Search and Destroy)."

      [/*]

    • Yaiba ASM-R250 Muramasa

      Reward from a new side job (to unlock, purchase 1 Yaiba vehicle, purchase at least 3 vehicles through AUTOFIXER, and complete Reported Crime: You Play with Fire...).

      If you fail the side job, the vehicle can later be purchased through AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]

    • Chevillon Legatus 450 Aquila

      Available for purchase on AUTOFIXER.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Introducing AutoDrive! This cutting-edge, autonomous driving feature will take you to your chosen destination (i.e. job objective or placed pin on the map). If you have no set destination, it will take you on a leisurely ride through the streets of Night City. Simply hop in any of your vehicles, make sure you're on a road, and hold G (PC) / Left Stick (consoles) to activate. This feature is disabled when you enter combat or when your vehicle is heavily damaged.

    [/*]

  • Implemented Cinematic Camera for AutoDrive. Hold Q (PC) / D-Pad Right (consoles) to activate. Sit back and enjoy cinematic views of Night City as you cruise toward your destination.

    [/*]

  • Self-driving Delamain cabs are now available on demand! Simply open the menu to call vehicles, then select "Delamain Cab" from the list to request a ride. This feature unlocks after completing the job Don't Lose Your Mind (regardless of outcome) and receiving a message from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ is now available for vehicles from partner brands, including motorcycles. Additionally, the infamous hacker known as Cosmetic_Troll exploited a vulnerability and created a cracked version of Rayfield's CrystalCoat™ technology for lower-end vehicles. Please note, however, that some models do not support the technology, such as heavily modded nomad vehicles and job-related vehicles.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color schemes did not work properly on the Mizutani Shion MZ1 and MZ2.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where unique color scheme could not be applied properly to the Villefort Deleon "Vindicator".

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Added 27 new NPCs that can be spawned in Photo Mode, including Rita Wheeler, the Cassel twins, fixers, Dum Dum, the iguana, Brendan, and more.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between alternative outfits for NPCs spawned in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • You can now switch between V's saved Wardrobe outfits in Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Added a confirmation pop-up when exiting Photo Mode to prevent accidental exits after setting up the perfect shot.

    [/*]

  • Added more customization options to the Look-At Camera feature, including an option for only the character's eyes to turn toward the camera instead of their entire body.

    [/*]

  • Added improvements to Lighting:

    • Lights now spawn around the camera instead of the player character.

      [/*]

    • Added an outline to the spotlight mesh and an indicator when it's off screen for better visibility.

      [/*]

    • Improved light movement speed on controllers.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Added multiple new stickers and frames, including iconic quotes and stylish overlays that let you turn your screenshots into Night City postcards – perfect for sharing memories from the City of Dreams.

    [/*]

  • Improved Depth of Field and moved it to the Camera tab.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Color Balance tab, allowing you to create your own custom filters.

    [/*]

  • Added a new Time and Weather tab:

    • Weather: includes rain, acid rain, fog, sandstorm, pollution, and sunny.

      [/*]

    • Time of Day: changes the time of day within Photo Mode.

      [/*]

    • Frame Forward: advances through an unlimited amount of frames to capture the perfect shot.

      [/*]

    • Game Speed: allows in-game time to progress while in Photo Mode."

      [/*]
    [/*]

Quality of Life & Accessibility

  • The game will now detect if the player is using inverted mouse button settings and automatically adjusts in-game button prompts accordingly.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to toggle aiming down sights in Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Jobs & Open World

  • Cyberpsycho Sighting: Bloody Ritual - the "Crack the ritualist's shard" objective now properly disappears from the Journal after completing the objective.

    [/*]

  • Sex on Wheels - now properly appears in the Journal after receiving the message from Jake Estevez.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where selecting a specific dialogue option in the conversation with Bree created a nameless, iconless item in the player's Inventory.

    [/*]

  • Shot by Both Sides - fixed an issue where the button to go to the lower level didn't appear on the elevator panel.

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where, when using a controller in Trauma Drama, the controllable character would default to shooting upwards instead of forward.

    [/*]

  • Players can now drop more Cyberware Capacity Shards if some within the intended drop limit were previously missed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing automatic weapons to fire slower than intended.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Official BARGHEST Tac Vest didn't drop from the scripted Airdrop as intended.

    [/*]

  • The level 60 Engineer perk no longer activates the EMP blast outside of combat or after entering a vehicle.

    [/*]

  • Added an option to replay the gameplay tutorial at any time via Settings → Controls.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Added an option to tell Johnny to go away after you look at him for a short while when he appears in the passenger seat. He takes the hint and disappears as a passenger for a couple days.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the sound of V's Radioport could be randomly interrupted by the Radioports of nearby NPCs.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where History by Gazelle Twin and Trash Generation played too loudly compared to other songs on the radio.

    [/*]

  • Improved the HDR Setting screen: fixed the HDR calibration preview so it correctly reflects the chosen settings, and clarified the description of the "Tone-Mapping Midpoint" setting.

    [/*]

  • Updated the End User Licence Agreement. You will be asked to accept it again when you load the game after updating.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several visual issues with missing, clipping, or floating textures.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several localization issues in various languages.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 4 for compatible AMD GPUs. IMPORTANT: The FSR 4 option will not be available in the in-game settings until the supporting AMD driver is installed. Please note that the driver will be released at a later date.

    [/*]

  • Added support for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution Frame Generation 3.1 for compatible hardware. It can now be used in combination with any upscaler.

    [/*]

  • Added support for ​Intel XeSS 2.0, with XeSS Frame Generation available on compatible hardware.

    [/*]

  • Added support for HDR10+ GAMING certified Intel GPUs. To enable this feature, your display must support the technology (find my display) and have "Game Mode" enabled. The HDR10+ GAMING toggle can be found in Settings in the Video tab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the DLSS Super Resolution Preset would invisibly revert from the CNN model to the Transformer model after restarting the game, even though the UI still displayed the CNN model as active.

    [/*]

  • Added more detailed information to the DLSS Super Resolution Preset tooltip in Settings to help players choose the best option for their setup.

    [/*]

  • Added the ability to move the mouse cursor to a different display while in Windowed Borderless mode.

    [/*]

  • Increased the maximum save size from 12 MB to 15 MB.

    [/*]

  • It will now be possible to rebind the key used to jump out of vehicles with the Stuntjock perk.

    [/*]
